main_body: A thin dark iron lamp post (a pole about 2px wide) with a T-shaped crossbar at the top, two hanging yellow lanterns, and a small grey stone base at the bottom.
top_band: none: the pole's column scan runs from a dark outline straight into a uniform dark shaft (rows 5-31, L 37-42). The only light rows are at the stone base, rows 32-38, and no cap surface is visible at the top.
evidence: The post is a slim dark shaft with a thin T-bar drawn straight from the front. The crossbar is a 1-2 row dark line with no top surface above it. The lanterns are flat front-view boxes. The post has no cap (no ellipse or plate wider than the shaft, nothing at least 4 rows tall and lighter than the shaft). The grey base at rows 32-38 has some lighter rows, but it is a small plinth and does not count for the main body. This matches the red flat-band/rim-only column in the guide.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 17 distinct colours against 38-40 in the references. The post shaft is a flat near-neutral dark grey with almost no shading. 99% of the dark edge pixels are neutral, which means a near-black outline rather than a tinted material tone. The lanterns have only 2-3 yellow tones and the stone base has a few grey steps. Compared with the richly textured stall and well, it looks thin and sticker-like. The 5x5 flat-fill figure is 0%, but only because the shapes are so thin that no 5x5 block fits.
